definition: Post-processing raw ASR output (which has neither) into readable, correctly punctuated text.
details: Post-processing raw ASR output (which has neither) into readable, correctly punctuated text. Essential for downstream NLP, subtitling, and summarization; typically a small sequence-labeling model over the transcript.

explainer.lead: It turns raw ASR output, which has neither punctuation nor casing, into readable, correctly punctuated text. It matters because downstream NLP, subtitling and summarization need structured, readable transcripts.

tiers.eli5: Speech recognition writes everything as a flat run of lowercase words, so this step adds capitals and punctuation.
tiers.practitioner: Typically implemented as a small sequence-labeling model over the transcript; the pitfall is that errors here propagate into every downstream task.
tiers.paperLevel: Post-processing of raw ASR output via a small sequence-labeling model over the transcript; no formula or accuracy bound is stated.

explainer.example: The raw output "we should leave now" is restored to "We should leave now."
